sentences.text: Wulatelong gobiensis is the only known species of this basal oviraptorid dinosaur, which lived during the Late Cretaceous.
As a member of the oviraptorid group, it possessed a bird-like body plan featuring a toothless, parrot-like beak and often bore elaborate crests.
A single nearly complete skeleton, cataloged as IVPP V 18409, was unearthed in 2009 within the Bayan Mandahu region of Inner Mongolia.
The genus was formally named by Xu and colleagues in 2013, combining the local place name Wulate with the Chinese character for dragon.

Taxonomically, Wulatelong belongs to the subfamily Citipatinae within the family Oviraptoridae, the infraorder Oviraptorosauria, the superfamily Caenagnathoidea, the theropod suborder Theropoda, the order Saurischia, the phylum Chordata, the class Sauropsida, and the kingdom Animalia.

Fossils are found in the Late Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation of Inner Mongolia, China, with estimates placing its life between 75 and 71 million years ago during the Campanian stage, though other estimates suggest a range from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
